1:8.t: "Meditate" (Hebrew hagah): the word means to murmur or speak under one's breath, as well as to think over. Reading aloud was normal, so the law that is "not to leave your mouth" is to be read over, repeated and pondered. The same word is used in Psalm 1:2.
"Succeed" (Hebrew sakal): the KJV's "have good success". The verb also means to act wisely, so success here is the result of living by wisdom from God's law, not good luck.

1:13.t: "Rest" (Hebrew nuach, menuchah): rest is a key word in Joshua. It means settled peace in the land, safe from enemies, the fulfillment of God's promise in Deuteronomy 12:9-10. Hebrews 4:8 builds on this to say that Joshua's rest pointed to a greater rest still to come.

2:12.t: "Kindness", "kindness and faithfulness" (Hebrew hesed, emet): see Genesis 24:27. Rahab, a Canaanite, appeals to hesed, the language of covenant loyalty, and the spies answer with the same pair of words that describes God's own character.

2:14.t: "Kindness", "kindness and faithfulness" (Hebrew hesed, emet): see Genesis 24:27. Rahab, a Canaanite, appeals to hesed, the language of covenant loyalty, and the spies answer with the same pair of words that describes God's own character.

6:17.t: "Devoted to the LORD for destruction" (Hebrew herem; verb haram): the KJV's "accursed". herem means something set apart wholly for God, taken out of human use, either by giving it to the sanctuary (the metals in 6:19) or by destroying it. In war it meant that a city and its people were not to be kept as plunder. The KJV renders it "accursed thing", "devoted thing" and, for the verb, "utterly destroy". We use "devoted to destruction" and "the devoted things", which keep both the religious and the destructive sides of the word. The same word is behind "utterly destroyed" in 2:10, 6:21, 8:26, 10:28-40 and 11:11-21.

7:12.t: "They themselves have become devoted to destruction": by taking what belonged to God under herem, Israel itself came under it (see 6:17). This is why Achan and all that was his are destroyed.

7:19.t: "Give glory to the LORD": a solemn call to tell the truth before God, used here as an oath formula, as in John 9:24.

22:22.t: "The LORD, the God of gods" (Hebrew El, Elohim, YHWH): the KJV's reading is kept. The Hebrew strings together three names for God, El, Elohim and YHWH, and many modern Bibles read them as a list: "The Mighty One, God, the LORD". Either way, saying it twice makes it a solemn oath.

24:15.t: "Serve" (Hebrew avad): the word means to work for, to serve as a slave, and to worship. Joshua's challenge uses it again and again in verses 14-24, and Israel has just been set free from "the house of slavery" (verse 17, from the same root). The choice is not between serving and freedom but between masters.
